cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

mechanism: Treat an evasive apology as a pupil's incomplete social lesson, eliciting ownership without ever naming the offense.
confusable: Not actual classroom coaching or an offense explanation: the corrections are A's interpersonal tactic and must focus on the apology's subject, leaving the grievance unnamed.
comparison: A warm tea ritual and corrected wording differ from a partner using text icons before visitors arrive.
seedUse: Retains usual mug, still-tea invitation and sorry-you-feel non-apology; makes the alleged lesson act on each response.
